name: Sodium-Ion Batteries: India's First Listed Cell & Pack Developers
scope: India's listed exposure to sodium-ion (Na-ion) cells and packs for stationary storage and data centres: Tata Chemicals (pack builder), KPIT (technology licensor), plus the few other listed names with a company-confirmed link, set against Chinese scale-up, LFP pricing and India's storage pilots and tenders.

summary.one_line: India's sodium-ion story is moving from lab to pilot (a Tata Chemicals pack in test, KPIT's technology licensed to an unlisted partner, and NTPC and Jaipur utility pilots out to tender), but listed exposure is narrow, unquantified and far too small to move either parent's earnings before FY29.
key_points: Tata Chemicals has built its first sodium-ion pack and is testing it. It expects the pilot phase to take 6-9 months and to have customer testing units by end-FY27. Accounts of the commercial-plant timing differ: one report says a plant 'within two years', another says two years after the pilot ends, roughly FY29-30 (S1, S2).

KPIT transferred its sodium-ion technology, developed with IISER Pune, to unlisted Trentar Energy in Feb 2025. Trentar is to build 3 GWh of annual capacity, and KPIT gets an upfront fee plus 8 years of royalties. Neither amount has been disclosed, and we found no public update on the plant's progress (S3, S4).

Demand-side pilots have started: NTPC sought expressions of interest (EoIs) for a grid-connected Na-ion battery storage (BESS) pilot on 10 Sep 2026 (S5), and Jaipur discom JVVNL and GEAPP issued an RfP for a 250 kW / 250 kWh distribution-transformer pilot on 29 Oct 2026 (S7).

The cost gap with LFP is narrowing but has not closed. Gasgoo, citing industry research, puts fully loaded Na-ion cell cost at 0.33-0.42 yuan/Wh against 0.33-0.34 yuan/Wh for LFP, with parity expected between late 2026 and 2027 (S9).
LFP keeps moving the goalposts: BNEF's 2025 survey put stationary-storage pack prices at $70/kWh, down 45% year on year, and it expects a further decline in 2026 (S10).

The addressable stationary market is large. India's BESS requirement is estimated at 236.22 GWh by FY2031-32, against 9.08 GWh operational in Aug 2026 (S11), and 30 GWh of standalone BESS has viability-gap funding (VGF, a capital subsidy) support (S12).

Neither stock has traded on the theme. KPIT fell ~16% to a 52-week low on 1 Jul 2026 after an auto-services profit warning (S13). Tata Chemicals was down ~28.6% over the year to 1 Sep 2026 (S14). We found no broker note grouping the two as a sodium-ion basket, and Ventura's Aug 2026 note on Indian Na-ion did not mention Tata Chemicals at all (S15).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Tata Chemicals, if its pilot converts: it is the only listed Indian company we found with an in-house Na-ion pack under test with power companies and data centres (S2). It is also a soda-ash producer, and soda ash is a Na-ion raw material (S1).
KPIT, through royalty income if Trentar's 3 GWh plant is built and sells (S3). The upside is pure licensing, with no capex required from KPIT.
Reliance Industries holds 100% of Faradion, a UK Na-ion developer, and plans to use its technology at the Jamnagar gigafactory (S16). Sodium-ion is a tiny part of a very large group.

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Falling LFP prices ($70/kWh stationary packs in 2025, S10) can keep pushing back the point at which Na-ion is cheaper.
Chinese scale: CATL expects its Na-ion cell cost to match LFP by end-2026 and system cost by 2027 (S24). Chinese scale could make imported Na-ion cells the price-setter in India.
Materiality: Tata Chemicals has disclosed no sodium-ion-specific capex and has not given a soda-ash-per-GWh figure (S2). KPIT's fee and royalty amounts are undisclosed (S3).
Partner dependence: KPIT's outcome depends on unlisted Trentar, whose plant status is not public (S3).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Completion of the Tata Chemicals pilot (6-9 months from Jul 2026) and customer testing units by end-FY27 (S1, S2).
Any Trentar site, construction or first-revenue announcement, and any royalty line in KPIT's results (S3).
Awards under NTPC's sodium-ion EoI and the JVVNL/GEAPP Jaipur RfP: which vendors win, and whether any is listed (S5, S7).
Naxion's 500 MWh pilot cell plant, planned by 2027 (S20), as a gauge of Indian cell-making readiness and possible partners for listed companies.

sections.title: What sodium-ion is and where it fits

blocks.text: Sodium-ion cells use sodium in place of lithium in the cathode, usually with a hard-carbon anode, so they need no lithium. Sodium is roughly 500 times more abundant than lithium (S15). The trade-off is energy density, which is lower than LFP's (S9). The advantages are cold-weather performance (over 90% capacity retention at -40°C in Chinese industry data), a higher thermal-runaway trigger temperature, and claimed cycle lives above 15,000 for some chemistries (S9). KPIT's own cells are rated at 100-170 Wh/kg and 80% capacity retention over 3,000-6,000 cycles (S4).

Realistic first markets are stationary: long-duration and cold-climate storage, data-centre backup and start-stop systems (S9). Tata Chemicals says its commercial focus is 'solely on stationary applications, not mobility' (S2). KPIT pitches 2/3/4-wheelers as well as UPS and grid storage (S3).

China leads. A CATL executive expects its sodium-ion cell cost to match LFP by end-2026, with full storage-system cost parity by 2027 (S24). The industry broadly expects cell cost parity with LFP between late 2026 and 2027, sooner if lithium carbonate stays expensive. Morgan Stanley projects Na-ion at about 2% of global installed battery capacity in 2027, 20% in 2030 and 37% in 2035 (S9).

LFP is a moving target. BNEF's 2025 survey found stationary-storage pack prices fell 45% to $70/kWh and LFP packs averaged $81/kWh across segments, and it expects packs to get cheaper again in 2026 (S10). Ventura cites industry estimates that Na-ion could reach roughly 10% of global storage additions by 2030 (S15). The spread between that and Morgan Stanley's 20% shows how wide the estimates are.

sections.title: India policy, pilots and the storage market

subsections.title: Policy: ACC PLI, VGF and Na-ion pilots

items: The ACC PLI scheme (₹18,100 crore outlay for 50 GWh) lets beneficiaries choose their technology. Ventura notes most allocated capacity has gone to lithium-ion because Na-ion's commercial path is uncertain (S15, S18).
Reliance New Energy Battery was awarded 10 GWh under the ACC PLI in Sep 2024 (S18). It is the only PLI beneficiary that also owns a Na-ion developer (S16).

The Ministry of Power approved VGF of INR 5,400 crore for 30 GWh of standalone BESS in Jun 2025: 25 GWh across 15 states and 5 GWh for NTPC (S12). The scheme does not ring-fence any sodium-ion capacity, so Na-ion has to compete with LFP on price.

NTPC EoI (10 Sep 2026): a grid-connected Na-ion BESS at thermal stations or offices. The reference size is 100 kWh usable, or bidders can propose their own. Applicants at TRL 4-5 must fund at least 50% of the cost (S5, S6).

JVVNL and GEAPP (29 Oct 2026): India's first distribution-transformer Na-ion pilot, 250 kW / 250 kWh, at K.L. Saini Stadium, Jaipur. It will test heat performance, thermal safety and lifecycle cost against Li-ion (S7).
The Renewable Energy Secretary said in Aug 2026 that Indian Na-ion research has reached TRL 7 (S23).

blocks.text: Rubix Data Sciences, drawing on National Electricity Plan estimates, puts India's BESS requirement at 236.22 GWh by FY2031-32, up from 34.72 GWh in FY2026-27, with INR 3.49 trillion of investment needed. Operational BESS was 9.08 GWh in Aug 2026, against a 176.66 GWh pipeline (S11). Even a single-digit Na-ion share of this would exceed the 3 GWh Trentar plant and Tata Chemicals' pilot scale.

blocks.text: Materiality is unquantifiable today. Tata Chemicals' Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell about ₹100 crore YoY on soda-ash headwinds (S2), and those soda-ash cycles drive the stock. KPIT's market cap of ~₹15,379 crore (Jul 2026, S13) is set by its auto-software services business. Neither company has disclosed Na-ion revenue guidance.

subsections.title: Other listed names and the unlisted field

items: Reliance Industries (large cap): RNEL owns 100% of Faradion, a UK Na-ion developer, and plans to use its technology at the Jamnagar storage gigafactory (S16). Reliance said in Aug 2024 that it would bring sodium-ion cell production to megawatt industrial scale the following year (S17). We found no 2026 production confirmation.
NTPC (large cap): a buyer and tester rather than a supplier. It is running the Na-ion BESS EoI (S5).

Waaree Technologies (BSE small cap): signed a non-binding MoU with Israel's 3DBattery in Nov 2023 covering Li-ion and 'upcoming' sodium-ion, with a 5 GWh cell ambition. We found no follow-up, so the link is weak (S19).

Unlisted developers: Naxion (1.5 GWh/yr pack capacity at Coimbatore; ₹200 crore, 500 MWh pilot cell plant planned by 2027) (S20); Epsilon Advanced Materials Pvt Ltd (coconut-shell hard-carbon anode, May 2026) (S21); INDI Energy and GODI Energy, which Ventura names as testing sodium-ion (S15). None has announced a partnership with a listed company or plans to list.

blocks.text: Market-cap gap: we found no listed small cap with company-confirmed, active sodium-ion work. Waaree Technologies' 2023 MoU is the closest and is non-binding. Mid- and small-cap exposure is genuinely absent at this stage, so we have not padded the list.

Mainstream coverage of these stocks as a sodium-ion group is minimal. Ventura's Aug 2026 note says India is 'in its infancy' on Na-ion versus China. It names KPIT and Reliance as testing sodium-ion and mentions Tata Group but not Tata Chemicals specifically. It also cites hopes of 20-30% cost savings at scale (S15). We found no broker initiation or price-target change tied to sodium-ion for either core name.

blocks.caption: Share-price moves and attributed drivers
rows: Q1 FY27 profit warning on European auto client slowdown; JPMorgan downgrade to Underweight
Soda-ash headwinds; no Na-ion-linked re-rating found

blocks.text: Brokers' sodium-ion views are mostly about global cost: Morgan Stanley (via Gasgoo) says Na-ion could be over 30% cheaper than LFP once capacity reaches 100 GWh, and projects a 20% share of global installed capacity by 2030 (S9). These are the brokers' forecasts, not ours.

items: LFP deflation: stationary packs at $70/kWh and still falling (S10) could keep pushing parity back beyond the industry's late-2026 to 2027 window (S9).
Chinese scale: CATL targets cell cost parity with LFP by end-2026 (S24), which could leave Indian pilots competing with low-cost imports.
Slow conversion from pilot to commercial scale: Tata Chemicals' own timeline puts full scale around FY29-30 (S2). The NTPC and Jaipur pilots are only at 100-250 kWh scale (S5, S7).
Immateriality: no Na-ion capex, revenue or royalty figures have been disclosed by either company (S2, S3).
Licensing dependence: KPIT's returns depend on Trentar, an unlisted partner, executing a plant for which we found no public status (S3).

companies.name: Tata Chemicals Ltd
companies.role: Has built its first sodium-ion pack and is testing a full indigenous unit with BMS with power companies and data centres; pilot due in 6-9 months from Jul 2026 (S1, S2).
companies.impact: A long-dated option. A commercial plant is roughly two years out, no Na-ion capex has been disclosed, and soda-ash cycles drive earnings (S1, S2).

companies.name: KPIT Technologies Ltd
companies.role: Developed Na-ion cell technology with IISER Pune (100-170 Wh/kg) (S4) and transferred it to Trentar Energy, which plans a 3 GWh/yr plant (S3).
companies.impact: Upfront fee plus 8-year royalty, amounts undisclosed. The stock is driven by its auto-software slowdown, not Na-ion (S3, S13).

companies.name: Reliance Industries Ltd
companies.role: Owns 100% of UK Na-ion developer Faradion via RNEL, for use at its Jamnagar storage gigafactory (S16); ACC PLI beneficiary (S18).
companies.impact: Has the largest potential Na-ion capability among listed Indian companies, but it is immaterial to group earnings and we found no 2026 production confirmation (S16, S17).

companies.name: NTPC Ltd
companies.role: Buyer and tester: issued an EoI for a grid-connected Na-ion BESS pilot at its plants and offices (S5, S6).
companies.impact: Its pilot results and award will signal utility appetite for Na-ion; not an earnings driver for NTPC (S5).

companies.name: Waaree Technologies Ltd
companies.role: Non-binding 2023 MoU with Israel's 3DBattery on Li-ion and upcoming Na-ion storage, with a 5 GWh cell ambition (S19).
companies.impact: Weak, unconfirmed exposure; no follow-up found since 2023. Watch-list only (S19).

method: First edition, researched on 2026-10-31 using web searches and fetches of company-linked, government/agency, trade-press and broker pages. The Tata Chemicals call details come from two secondary summaries of the 27 Jul 2026 Q1 FY27 call, not the company transcript, which we could not retrieve; where they differ on plant timing, both versions are shown. The KPIT NSE investor presentation timed out and was not used. We screened the listed universe for company-confirmed sodium-ion activity across large, mid and small caps and found only Reliance, NTPC (as buyer) and a non-binding Waaree Technologies MoU beyond the two core names; names linked only by adjacency are flagged as watch-only. Share-price data are the latest dated figures found (Jul-Sep 2026); the dashboard's numbers.json supplies current screener data. No ratings or price targets are given. BSE codes are shown only where a source confirmed them.
